guard_streams.source: 1.6 million Brits hit switch on their landline or broadband provider
guard_streams.write_limit: Switching adoption, provider participation and contract savings are market-process evidence, not parcel coverage or measured performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the One Touch Switch anniversary update on 12 September 2025.
The update marked one year since the process launched.
More than 1.6 million customers had switched landline or broadband provider.
More than 300 providers were signed up to One Touch Switch.
Customers only need to contact the provider they want to join.
The process supports switching between providers using different networks.
Providers must coordinate the date so notice-period charges do not continue beyond the switch.
Customers may receive compensation for delayed starts or loss of service longer than one working day.
Ofcom reported 36% of fixed broadband and landline bundle customers were out of contract at the end of June 2024.
Those dual-play out-of-contract bills were 18% higher than in-contract bills.

guard_streams.source: Checklist for new phone or broadband contract
guard_streams.write_limit: Contract duration, pricing and cancellation guidance do not verify physical network coverage or selected-parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the contract checklist on 22 January 2014.
The checklist was last updated on 26 June 2026.
The guidance covers residential and small-business customers with ten employees or fewer.
Some contracts operate on a month-to-month rolling basis.
Other contracts may have 12, 18 or 24-month minimum terms.
Providers must offer an option no longer than 12 months for each service.
Residential and small-business service contracts should not exceed 24 months.
A handset agreement can be longer if it is separate from the airtime contract.
The airtime contract cannot exceed 24 months.
Customers should review price-increase and termination terms before signing.

guard_streams.source: Signal struggles on trains widespread, Ofcom research finds
guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile rail-route measurements are not fixed-broadband parcel coverage or measured selected-parcel speed evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the train-connectivity research on 3 June 2026.
The research measured 24 segments of key railway lines.
The measured routes covered England, Scotland and Wales.
Good performance required at least 5 Mbit/s download, 1.5 Mbit/s upload and latency no more than 50 ms.
EE met the good-performance threshold on 42% of measured segments.
Three met the threshold on 21% of measured segments.
O2 met the threshold on 20% of measured segments.
Vodafone met the threshold on 17% of measured segments.
On-board Wi-Fi performed well only 1% of the time.
Ofcom said UK mobile networks had invested £10 billion since 2020.

guard_streams.source: Choosing the best mobile, broadband and landline provider
guard_streams.write_limit: Provider comparison and satisfaction data are service-quality context and cannot establish selected-parcel coverage or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the provider comparison page on 12 April 2017.
The page was last updated on 10 February 2026.
Ofcom states that it wants users to get the best from phones and broadband.
The comparison uses information collected from residential customers and providers.
The information is used to build a picture of UK service quality.
The page provides an interactive provider performance report.
The report supports mobile provider comparison.
The report supports home-broadband provider comparison.
The report supports landline provider comparison.
Definitions and methodology are linked through the full Comparing Customer Service report.

guard_streams.source: Investigation into BT's compliance with statutory requests for information
guard_streams.write_limit: An open statutory-information investigation concerns regulatory compliance and does not verify selected-parcel broadband coverage or performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the BT investigation page on 29 April 2026.
The investigation is open.
The investigated company is British Telecommunications PLC.
The relevant legal provision is section 137A of the Communications Act 2003.
The investigation concerns compliance with statutory information-request notices.
The information was provided by BT entities EE Limited and Plusnet Plc.
Ofcom issued formal notices on 7 December 2023.
The requested information supported Ofcom's statutory consumer functions.
The information was intended to inform the 2025 Comparing Customer Service report.
The open investigation page does not record a final breach finding.
